mainTopic: Which תנא holds זה וזה גורם אסור; רבי אליעזר's view; אביי on ovens, pots and pottery; שמואל's reversed version; and bread baked over coals of forbidden wood.
overview: Something can come about through two causes at once, one forbidden and one permitted. This is called זה וזה גורם. The גמרא is searching for a תנא who agrees with רבי that such a result is forbidden, as in bread baked in an oven heated with forbidden fuel. A first proof from רבי אליעזר, about forbidden and permitted starter in dough, is rejected, because he may simply follow the last ingredient. A second proof comes from the משנה about אשירה wood. רבי אליעזר argues only about a mixture of the bread, and a ברייתא confirms that he was strict in all Torah prohibitions. אביי then explains the dispute between רבי and חכמים: pottery fired with forbidden wood is forbidden by everyone, while an oven or pot depends on the זה וזה גורם question. שמואל teaches the ברייתא with the names reversed, and the גמרא explains why. Finally, bread cooked on coals is permitted, two אמוראים argue about glowing coals, and רב פפא says רבי forbids the bread when a flame burns directly opposite it.

steps.title: End of the sourdough source and אביי's explanation of רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The quoted ברייתא ends with the חכמים: the dough is forbidden only if the forbidden starter alone could leaven it. אביי explains that רבי אליעזר permits the dough when the permitted starter fell in last only if the forbidden starter was removed first. This shows that when both causes work together, the dough is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: '...until there is enough in it to make the dough rise.' And אביי said: רבי אליעזר only taught this when the person first removed the forbidden starter. But if he did not first remove it, the dough is forbidden. So we see that when both of them cause the rising, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the source about forbidden and permitted starter falling into dough. Then it brings אביי's explanation, which seems to prove that רבי אליעזר holds זה וזה גורם אסור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר said 'I follow the last ingredient,' so if the permitted starter fell in last, the dough is permitted. אביי limits this: it applies only when the forbidden starter was taken out before the permitted one made the dough rise. If the forbidden starter stayed in and both worked together, the dough is forbidden. That is exactly the rule זה וזה גורם אסור.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this and that cause it: a result produced by a forbidden cause and a permitted cause together
To make dough rise and become חמץ
They only taught this when: a formula that limits a ruling to a specific case
Apparently / so we see: introduces a conclusion drawn from what was just said

steps.confusionAlert: The opening words 'עד שיהא בו כדי להחמיץ' belong to the חכמים, the last speakers in the quoted ברייתא. אביי's comment, however, is about רבי אליעזר's view.

phrases.english: until there is enough in it to cause leavening.
phrases.notes: This is where the חכמים's words in the ברייתא being quoted come to an end.

phrases.english: And Abaye said:
They taught this only
phrases.notes: He means רבי אליעזר's lenient ruling, where the permitted starter fell in last.

phrases.english: where he first removed the forbidden item,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא קָדַם וְסִילֵּק אֶת הָאִיסּוּר — אָסוּר,
phrases.english: but if he did not first remove the forbidden item, it is forbidden,
apparently, when both this and that cause it, it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the proof attempt begun on the previous amud, which quoted the starter ברייתא as a source for זה וזה גורם אסור.
steps.raayaObject: That some תנא, namely רבי אליעזר, holds זה וזה גורם אסור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about starter falling into dough, as explained by אביי.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's reason may simply be that the last ingredient decides
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Perhaps רבי אליעזר's whole reason is 'I follow the last ingredient.' Then removing the forbidden starter would not matter. And if both fell in at the same moment, he would actually permit the dough.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that רבי אליעזר's reason matches אביי's explanation? Maybe his reason is 'I go after the last one.' Then it makes no difference whether he removed the forbidden starter first or not. But if both fell in at once, he might indeed permit it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from step 1. It suggests a different reason for רבי אליעזר's ruling, one that has nothing to do with זה וזה גורם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי אליעזר simply follows whichever ingredient came last, then the question of removing the forbidden starter is irrelevant. His ruling would tell us nothing about two causes working together. In fact, when both fall in at the same time and there is no 'last' one, he might hold זה וזה גורם מותר. So the source cannot prove that anyone holds זה וזה גורם אסור.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where (do we know)? Challenges an assumption
I follow the last one: רבי אליעזר's principle that the last ingredient decides

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying אביי is wrong about the law. It is only saying that רבי אליעזר's words do not force אביי's reading, so the source cannot serve as proof.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that Rabbi Eliezer's reason is like Abaye's?
Perhaps Rabbi Eliezer's reason
is because 'I follow the last one,'

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁנָא קָדַם וְסִילֵּק אֶת הָאִיסּוּר,
phrases.english: and it makes no difference whether he first removed the forbidden item,

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁנָא לֹא קָדַם וְסִילֵּק אֶת הָאִיסּוּר.
phrases.english: or whether he did not first remove the forbidden item.
But if they fell in at the same time,
indeed it would be permitted!
phrases.notes: In that case רבי אליעזר might hold זה וזה גורם מותר: when a permitted cause and a forbidden cause work together, the result is allowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The entire proof from the starter case for זה וזה גורם אסור.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי אליעזר's ruling can be explained by 'the last ingredient decides,' which ignores the issue of two causes together. When both fall in at once, he might even permit the dough.

steps.title: A new source: רבי אליעזר and wood from an אשירה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a different source from רבי אליעזר: the משנה about wood taken from an אשירה. The wood is forbidden for benefit. An oven heated with it must be broken if new, or cooled down if old.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the source is רבי אליעזר in the case of אשירה wood, as we learned in a משנה: If someone took wood from it, the wood is forbidden for any benefit. If he heated an oven with it, a new oven must be smashed and an old oven must be cooled.
steps.whatsHappening: Having dropped the first proof, the גמרא opens a new attempt using the אשירה wood case. This step lays out the first part of that משנה to set up the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heat from the first firing completes a new oven, so the oven itself has gained from the forbidden wood. That is why it must be destroyed. An old oven is already finished and only received forbidden heat, so it is enough to let it cool. This background prepares for the bread case in the next lines, which is where the זה וזה גורם question arises.

keyTerms.meaning: A tree worshipped as an idol

phrases.english: Rather, it is Rabbi Eliezer of the asheira wood,
as we learned in a Mishnah:
If one took wood from it, the wood is forbidden for benefit.
If he heated the oven with them,
if it is new, it must be smashed,
phrases.notes: The first firing completes a new oven, so the oven benefited from the forbidden wood.

phrases.english: if it is old, it must be cooled.
phrases.notes: Only the forbidden heat has to be removed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר דַּעֲצֵי אֲשֵׁירָה, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the starter proof was rejected, the גמרא replaces it with a new source from the same תנא.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר holds זה וזה גורם אסור.

steps.title: Bread baked with אשירה wood, and mixtures of that bread
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues. Bread baked in an oven heated with אשירה wood is forbidden for benefit. If it gets mixed with other loaves, and those with still others, all of them are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he baked bread in it, it is forbidden for benefit. If that bread got mixed with other loaves, and those with other loaves, all of them are forbidden for benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the משנה, now reaching the bread case. This is the heart of the proof being set up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bread was produced by two causes together: the fire of the forbidden wood and the permitted oven. That is a classic זה וזה גורם case, yet the תנא קמא rules the bread forbidden. He is so strict that even a mixture spreading through many loaves is entirely forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: אָפָה בּוֹ אֶת הַפַּת — אֲסוּרִין בַּהֲנָאָה.
phrases.english: If he baked bread in it, it is forbidden for benefit.
phrases.notes: The bread comes from both the forbidden wood's fire and the oven: זה וזה גורם.

phrases.english: If it became mixed with others,
and those others with other ones,
all of them are forbidden for benefit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָפָה בּוֹ אֶת הַפַּת — אֲסוּרִין בַּהֲנָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the same משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That bread produced by forbidden wood together with a permitted oven is forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The bread clause of the עצי אשירה משנה.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's dispute only concerns the mixture
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says the person can throw the value of the benefit into the ים המלח, so the whole mixture does not have to be destroyed. The חכמים answer that עבודה זרה cannot be redeemed with money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: He should take the value of the benefit and throw it into the ים המלח. They said to him: There is no redemption for עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with רבי אליעזר's disagreement and the חכמים's reply. The גמרא is setting up its point: רבי אליעזר argues only about the mixture, not about whether the bread itself is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's solution is to destroy money equal to the wood's value instead of destroying all the bread. He never says the baked bread itself is permitted. That implies he agrees the bread, a זה וזה גורם product, is forbidden. The חכמים reject paying off the benefit, because עבודה זרה cannot be released through money.

keyTerms.meaning: He brings the value of the benefit to the Dead Sea, meaning he destroys an equivalent amount of money
Redemption: transferring a prohibition onto money
Idol worship, or items connected to it

steps.whatToRemember: The first proof, from starter in dough, failed because רבי אליעזר might simply follow the last ingredient. The new proof comes from אשירה wood. Bread baked with it is a זה וזה גורם product, and רבי אליעזר argues only about how to handle a mixture of that bread. So he too treats the bread itself as forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the גמרא's conclusion that even רבי אליעזר holds זה וזה גורם אסור. That rule matters for deciding when a mixed-cause result is permitted.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
He should bring the benefit to the Dead Sea.
phrases.notes: He destroys money equal to the wood's value, and the mixture becomes permitted.

phrases.english: They said to him:
There is no redemption for idolatry.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: יוֹלִיךְ הֲנָאָה לְיָם הַמֶּלַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה, giving the dispute that the proof depends on.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר agrees the bread itself, a זה וזה גורם product, is forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אליעזר disagrees only about the mixture, by paying off the benefit, and not about the bread's own status.

steps.title: Maybe רבי אליעזר is strict only about עבודה זרה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from the אשירה wood. Maybe רבי אליעזר forbids a mixture only because עבודה זרה is an especially severe prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fine, you heard רבי אליעזר say this about עבודה זרה, whose prohibition is severe. But did you hear him say it about the other prohibitions in the Torah?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from Step 5. A rule about עבודה זרה may not carry over to other prohibitions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עבודה זרה is treated with extra strictness. So רבי אליעזר's strictness there might be special to it. If so, we cannot learn from it about ordinary prohibitions like ערלה and כלאי הכרם, the subject of רבי's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Say / perhaps. It introduces a limiting suggestion.
The other prohibitions of the Torah

phrases.english: Say that you heard Rabbi Eliezer hold this
regarding idolatry, whose prohibition is severe;
regarding the other prohibitions in the Torah,
did you hear him say it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימוֹר דְּשָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought from the אשירה משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The extension of רבי אליעזר's ruling from עבודה זרה to all prohibitions.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case of עבודה זרה may be uniquely strict, so it cannot serve as a general model.

steps.title: Then who else could the ברייתא follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that if רבי אליעזר were not the author of the strict view on ordinary prohibitions, there would be no one else to attribute it to.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if that is so, to whom will you attribute the ברייתא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the proof. The whole search began because רבי, in the ברייתא quoted on the previous amud about an oven heated with עָרְלָה peels or כִּלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם straw, forbids the bread. If רבי אליעזר is not strict outside עבודה זרה, there is no תנא who agrees with רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's ruling concerns ordinary Torah prohibitions, namely ערלה and כלאי הכרם, not עבודה זרה. If רבי אליעזר's strictness were limited to עבודה זרה, רבי's view would have no supporting תנא. So the גמרא insists that רבי אליעזר applies זה וזה גורם אסור to other prohibitions as well.

keyTerms.meaning: On whom will you place it? (To whom will you attribute it?)

phrases.english: But if so,
to whom will you attribute it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the דחיה of Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attribution argument: no other author fits.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר's strictness may be limited to עבודה זרה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אליעזר must hold זה וזה גורם אסור for ordinary prohibitions as well. Otherwise no תנא would support רבי's ruling forbidding bread baked with ערלה or כלאים fuel.

steps.title: An explicit ברייתא: רבי אליעזר forbade in all prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a direct source. A ברייתא states openly that רבי אליעזר applied this strictness to every Torah prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Moreover, it was taught explicitly: and so too רבי אליעזר would forbid in all the prohibitions of the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, stronger support. It is an explicit ברייתא that settles the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 was only an argument from attribution. Here a ברייתא says outright that רבי אליעזר was strict in all prohibitions. So the attempt to limit him to עבודה זרה is fully refuted.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר holds זה וזה גורם אסור in all Torah prohibitions, not only in עבודה זרה.

phrases.english: And furthermore, it was taught explicitly:
And so too Rabbi Eliezer would forbid
in all the prohibitions of the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an explicit source to reinforce the answer of Step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר applies זה וזה גורם אסור to all prohibitions.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: וכן היה רבי אליעזר אוסר בכל איסורין שבתורה.

steps.title: אביי: if רבי holds that two causes forbid, he agrees with רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: אביי begins analyzing רבי's ruling that bread baked in an oven heated with forbidden wood is forbidden. If רבי's reason is זה וזה גורם אסור, then his view is the same as רבי אליעזר's.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: If you say that 'this and that cause, it is forbidden,' then רבי is the same as רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי opens a two-sided analysis of רבי's opinion about the bread. This is the first side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bread is produced by two causes: the forbidden wood's heat and the permitted oven. If רבי forbids whenever two causes combine, his view matches רבי אליעזר exactly. Nothing new needs to be explained.

keyTerms.meaning: If you will say (introducing one of two possibilities)
This and that cause: a result produced by a forbidden and a permitted factor together

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'רבי' alone means רבי יהודה הנשיא, a different person from רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
If you will say
"this and that cause, it is forbidden":
Rabbi is the same as Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אִם תִּמְצָא לוֹמַר זֶה וָזֶה גּוֹרֵם אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having established רבי אליעזר's general view, אביי compares רבי's ruling to it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If רבי holds זה וזה גורם אסור, his ruling on the bread is identical to רבי אליעזר's view.

steps.title: If two causes are permitted, רבי forbids because the wood's benefit is in the bread
steps.stepSummary: אביי's second possibility: רבי holds זה וזה גורם מותר. He forbids the bread only because the wood's improvement goes directly into it. On that reasoning, pottery fired with forbidden wood is certainly forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say 'this and that cause, it is permitted,' and here רבי forbids because the improvement from the wood is in the bread itself, then these bowls, cups and flasks are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the other side of his analysis. He explains a different reason for רבי and shows what follows from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this view, two causes together do not forbid. רבי forbids the bread only because the forbidden wood's heat improved the bread directly. Clay bowls, cups and flasks fired with that wood are also directly improved by it, so they are forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The improvement that comes from the wood

phrases.english: And if you will say
"this and that cause, it is permitted,"

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכָא מִשּׁוּם דְּיֵשׁ שֶׁבַח עֵצִים בְּפַת הוּא —
phrases.english: and here it is because the improvement from the wood is in the bread:
then these bowls, cups and flasks are forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תִּמְצֵי לוֹמַר זֶה וָזֶה גּוֹרֵם מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second side of אביי's two-sided analysis.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under זה וזה גורם מותר, רבי forbids because of direct improvement from the wood. Therefore pottery fired with forbidden wood is forbidden.

steps.title: The real argument is about an oven and a pot
steps.stepSummary: אביי identifies where the two views actually disagree: an oven or pot that was fired with forbidden wood and is later used with permitted fuel.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where they argue is about an oven and a pot. According to the one who says 'this and that cause, forbidden,' it is forbidden. According to the one who says 'this and that cause, permitted,' it is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pinpoints the case that splits the two views.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An oven or pot fired with forbidden wood helps cook food only when permitted wood is burned later. So the cooking has two causes: the forbidden firing and the permitted fuel. Whoever forbids two causes forbids the oven and pot, and whoever permits two causes allows them.
steps.whatToRemember: Pottery is directly improved by forbidden wood, so it is forbidden. An oven or pot works only together with later permitted fuel, so it depends on the זה וזה גורם debate.

phrases.english: Where they argue is about an oven and a pot:

phrases.aramaic: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר ״זֶה וָזֶה גּוֹרֵם אָסוּר״ — אָסוּר.
phrases.english: according to the one who says "this and that cause, forbidden," it is forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר ״זֶה וָזֶה גּוֹרֵם מוּתָּר״ — שְׁרֵי.
phrases.english: According to the one who says "this and that cause, permitted," it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After naming a case everyone forbids, אביי names the case under dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An oven or pot fired with forbidden wood is forbidden under זה וזה גורם אסור and permitted under זה וזה גורם מותר.

steps.title: Second version: the pot is forbidden even for the lenient view
steps.stepSummary: A second version (איכא דאמרי) holds that even under זה וזה גורם מותר the pot is forbidden. It receives the food's cooking before any permitted wood is added.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: even according to the one who says 'this and that cause, permitted,' the pot is forbidden, because it receives the cooking before the permitted wood is put in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another version of אביי's teaching, which treats the pot differently from the oven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food is placed in the pot before the permitted wood is lit. So the forbidden pot is already being used on its own, with no permitted cause yet involved. That is not a case of two causes at all, so even the lenient view forbids it. Only the oven remains in dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: It received the cooking (it held the food)

steps.whatToRemember: In the second version, the oven depends on the זה וזה גורם debate, but the pot is forbidden according to everyone.

phrases.english: Some say:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ לְמַאן דְּאָמַר ״זֶה וָזֶה גּוֹרֵם מוּתָּר״,
phrases.english: even according to the one who says "this and that cause, permitted,"
the pot is forbidden,
since it receives the cooking
before the permitted wood is put in.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: אֲפִילּוּ לְמַאן דְּאָמַר זֶה וָזֶה גּוֹרֵם מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different version that takes the pot out of the dispute of Step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even under זה וזה גורם מותר, a pot fired with forbidden wood is forbidden, because it holds the food before the permitted fuel is added.

steps.title: שמואל's ruling on an oven heated with forbidden fuel
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that a new oven heated with עָרְלָה peels or כִּלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם straw must be smashed, and an old one must be cooled. On bread baked in it, רבי permits and חכמים forbid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said in the name of רב יהודה, who said in the name of שמואל: If someone heated an oven with peels of עָרְלָה fruit, or with straw of כִּלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם, then a new oven must be smashed and an old oven must be cooled. If he baked bread in it, רבי says the bread is permitted, and חכמים say the bread is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings שמואל's teaching about an oven heated with forbidden fuel. It also gives his version of the dispute over bread baked in such an oven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A new oven is finished and hardened by its first heating, so the forbidden fuel becomes part of the oven itself. That is why it must be smashed, just like the pottery case in אביי's analysis. An old oven was already finished, so letting it cool removes the forbidden heat. Notice that here רבי permits the bread and חכמים forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit (and its peels) from a tree's first three years, which is forbidden even for benefit
Grain or vegetables planted together with grapevines, which are forbidden even for benefit
He heated it (lit a fire in it)

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the names. In שמואל's version רבי is the one who PERMITS the bread. In the ברייתא discussed earlier (step 9), רבי FORBIDS it. The very next step points out this reversal.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said that Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
An oven that one heated with peels of orlah fruit,
or with straw of forbidden vineyard mixtures,
if it is new, it must be smashed;
phrases.notes: Its first firing finishes making it, so the forbidden fuel is built into it.

phrases.english: if it is old, it must be cooled.
If he baked bread in it,
Rebbi says: The bread is permitted,
and the Sages say: The bread is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings שמואל's version of the ברייתא about an oven heated with forbidden fuel, in which the opinions of רבי and חכמים appear reversed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A new oven heated with forbidden fuel is smashed and an old one is cooled. On the bread, רבי permits and חכמים forbid.

steps.title: The ברייתא teaches the opposite
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the known ברייתא assigns the opinions the other way around.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't the opposite taught?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל. The ברייתא we know says רבי forbids the bread, not that he permits it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier (steps 9 to 12) אביי analyzed רבי as the one who forbids the bread. שמואל's version swaps the opinions, so the גמרא wants to know why.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught (in a ברייתא)?
A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

phrases.english: But wasn't the reverse taught!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the way שמואל assigns the opinions in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's statement that רבי permits and חכמים forbid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The established ברייתא says the reverse: רבי forbids and חכמים permit.

steps.title: שמואל has a different version of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: Answer: שמואל simply learned the ברייתא with the opinions reversed.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל teaches it the reverse way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that שמואל had a different text of the ברייתא, in which the names are switched.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer does not claim the other version is wrong. It only says שמואל's tradition of the ברייתא was different, so there is no contradiction within his own words.

keyTerms.meaning: He teaches; he recites the text
A version or reading of a text
A leading אמורא of Bavel, of the first generation

phrases.english: Shmuel teaches it the reverse way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 14.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל's text of the ברייתא had the opinions reversed.

steps.title: שמואל deliberately reversed the names to guide the ruling
steps.stepSummary: Second answer: שמואל knew the standard version but swapped the names on purpose. That way the majority (רבנן) would appear to forbid, which matches the true הלכה in this case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you prefer, say this: In general שמואל holds that the הלכה follows רבי against one colleague but not against several colleagues. In this case, though, the הלכה follows רבי even against several colleagues. So שמואל decided to teach it reversed, so that רבנן would stand on the side of the prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer. שמואל accepted the normal text but changed it on purpose, so people would end up following the strict ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the הלכה follows רבי against one opponent, but not against a group. Here, though, the הלכה follows רבי even against the group, and רבי's real view forbids the bread. People might wrongly follow the majority and permit it. So שמואל put the strict ruling in the mouth of the majority, which leads people to the correct הלכה of forbidding the bread.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (introduces an alternative answer)
On the side of the prohibition
I will teach it (in a certain way)

steps.confusionAlert: In this answer, the real view of רבי is that the bread is forbidden. שמואל switched the names only so that the forbidding opinion would look like the majority. This is a teaching device; it is not a disagreement about what רבי held.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that an אמורא could adjust how a teaching is presented in order to steer people to the correct הלכה. In practice, the bread is forbidden.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
In general, Shmuel holds
that the halacha follows Rebbi against one colleague
but not against his several colleagues;
but in this case, even against his several colleagues.
And he reasoned: I will teach it reversed,
so that the Rabbis will stand on the side of the prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to step 14, different from the answer in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Intentional reversal for practical halachic guidance
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל must have had a different text.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל knew the standard text and reversed it on purpose, so people would follow the strict ruling, which is the true הלכה here.

steps.title: Bread cooked on the coals is permitted by everyone
steps.stepSummary: If the bread was cooked on coals of the forbidden wood rather than in its fire, all opinions agree it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he cooked the bread on top of coals, everyone agrees the bread is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a case everyone agrees on. Bread cooked on coals left from the forbidden wood is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the wood has turned into coals, it is no longer seen as the wood itself. So even רבי, who forbids bread baked with the wood's fire, agrees here. This sets up the next question: which kind of coals?

phrases.english: If he cooked it on top of coals,
all agree the bread is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the coals case to the ruling about bread.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bread cooked on coals of forbidden wood is permitted according to everyone.

steps.title: Dispute over dim coals versus glowing coals
steps.stepSummary: שמואל and רבי יוחנן disagree. One limits the leniency to dim coals and forbids bread on glowing coals. The other permits it even on glowing coals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in שמואל's name, and רבי חייא בר אשי said in רבי יוחנן's name. One said: They only taught this about dim coals, but glowing coals forbid the bread. The other said: Even glowing coals are permitted too.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים argue about how far the coals leniency goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dim coals have almost no fire left. Glowing coals are still hot and burning. The question is whether glowing coals are still close enough to the forbidden wood to pass its benefit into the bread.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this about... (limits a ruling)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: and Rabbi Chiya bar Ashi said that Rabbi Yochanan said;

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא גֶּחָלִים עוֹמְמוֹת,
phrases.english: one said: They taught this only about dim coals,
but with glowing coals, the bread is forbidden;

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ גֶּחָלִים לוֹחֲשׁוֹת נָמֵי מוּתָּרִין.
phrases.english: and one said: Even with glowing coals, it is also permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the limits of the coals ruling in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One view: only dim coals are permitted. Other view: even glowing coals are permitted.

steps.title: When does רבי's reason ever apply?
steps.stepSummary: If even glowing coals do not pass on the wood's benefit, when would רבי ever forbid bread because the wood's benefit is in it?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the one who says glowing coals forbid the bread, because the benefit of the wood is in the bread. But for the one who says even glowing coals are permitted, how can you find a case where רבי forbids bread because the benefit of the wood is in it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the lenient view. That view seems to leave no real case for רבי's reason for forbidding the bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bread is baked after the oven fire has died down, so it is really baked by the heat of coals. If even glowing coals do not count as giving the wood's benefit, it seems there is never a case where the wood itself benefits the bread. Then רבי's ruling would have nothing to apply to.

keyTerms.meaning: It is understandable (opens a contrast with a difficulty)
The benefit of the wood is in the bread
How can you find such a case?

phrases.english: It is understandable for the one who says glowing coals are forbidden,
because the benefit of the wood is in the bread.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר אֲפִילּוּ לוֹחֲשׁוֹת מוּתָּרוֹת,
phrases.english: But for the one who says even glowing coals are permitted,

phrases.aramaic: פַּת דְּאָסַר דְּיֵשׁ שֶׁבַח עֵצִים בַּפַּת לְרַבִּי
phrases.english: the bread that Rebbi forbids because the wood's benefit is in it,
how can you find such a case?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the lenient opinion in step 18, using רבי's reasoning from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that even glowing coals are permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Bread is always baked with coals. So if coals never pass on the wood's benefit, רבי's reason for forbidding the bread could never apply.

steps.title: רב פפא: a flame burning opposite the bread
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that רבי's case is when a live flame burns opposite the bread, so the wood's fire bakes it directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It is when a torch-like flame is burning opposite it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the case where רבי's reason applies: an actual flame of the forbidden wood burns facing the bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the lenient view in step 18, coals, even glowing ones, are no longer counted as the wood. A burning flame is the wood itself giving benefit. So when the flame faces the bread, the forbidden wood directly improves it, and רבי forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, student of אביי and רבא

steps.whatToRemember: An oven heated with forbidden fuel: a new one is smashed and an old one is cooled. Bread cooked on coals is permitted. According to the view that even glowing coals are permitted, רבי forbids the bread only when the forbidden wood's flame directly faces it, because then the wood's benefit is in the bread.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
When a flame is burning opposite it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If even glowing coals are permitted, רבי's prohibition could never apply.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי's prohibition applies when the flame of the forbidden wood directly faces the bread.
